messages.content: What are the most common chords in a pop song?

function.name: music_theory_primary_triads

message.content:
In most pop songs the harmonic palette is pretty tight and revolves around a handful of diatonic triads.  The “core” set that shows up in the majority of contemporary pop tracks is:

| Function | Roman‑numeral | Common chord names (in C major) |
|----------|---------------|--------------------------------|
| Tonic    | I             | C major (C–E–G)                |
| Subdominant | IV         | F major (F–A–C)                |
| Dominant | V             | G major (G–B–D)                |
| Relative minor | vi     | A minor (A–C–E)                |
| Supertonic | ii          | D minor (D–F–A)                |
| Mediant | iii            | E minor (E–G–B)                |

These six chords (I, ii, iii, IV, V, vi) cover the vast majority of pop progressions.  In practice, many songs will use only a subset of them—often just I–IV–V–vi or I–V–vi–IV.  Occasionally the ii or iii chords appear as passing or secondary chords, but the four main ones (I, IV, V, vi) are the backbone of pop harmony.
